record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a universal integer N such that every finite connected irreducible embedded geodesic net in Euclidean 3-space whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices, where edges are straight-line segments, intersections away from common endpoints are disallowed, balanced vertices satisfy the zero-sum unit-tangent condition, and irreducible means no proper edge subgraph is a geodesic net with the same unbalanced vertices?

evidence.quote: when 4 unbalanced vertices are non co-planar points in the Euclidean 3-space, e.g. the vertices of the regular tetrahedron.
Problem 3.2.3. Is there a number N such that each irreducible geodesic net with unbalanced vertices at all vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the set of four vertices of a regular tetrahedron. An embedded geodesic net with unbalanced vertices $T$ is a finite connected graph $G$ embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that: (i) each edge of $G$ is a straight-line segment; (ii) distinct edges meet only at common endpoints (no improper intersections); (iii) the vertex set of $G$ contains $T$; and (iv) at every vertex $v \notin T$ (a "balanced" vertex), the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$ equals the zero vector. Call such a net irreducible if no proper subgraph (obtained by removing at least one edge) that still contains $T$ is itself an embedded geodesic net with unbalanced-vertex set $T$ (i.e., still has every non-$T$ vertex balanced).

Question: Does there exist an integer $N$, independent of the net, such that every irreducible embedded geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with unbalanced vertices exactly equal to the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most $N$ balanced vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous problem for four boundary vertices in the plane has seen progress (constructions raising the known lower bound from 16 to 25 balanced vertices, with suggestions that the count may be unbounded), but no upper bound or unboundedness proof is established for the 3-dimensional regular-tetrahedron case. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs an irreducible geodesic net with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices, raising the prior maximum from 16, and suggests possible unboundedness.
status_evidence.claim: Related four-boundary-vertex problem is being actively studied with no definitive upper bound or unboundedness proof yet.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: For three boundary vertices, at most one balanced vertex can occur; four-boundary-vertex case behaves very differently.
status_evidence.claim: Three-boundary case resolved; four-boundary case (including the tetrahedral 3D version) remains open.
